game_identity.work_title: Sherlock Holmes versus Jack the Ripper

dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 8 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: The investigation centres on examining Whitechapel murder scenes, interviewing witnesses, reconstructing timelines and drawing deductions from physical clues and inventory puzzles.
Player-controlled Sherlock and Watson work through successive authored leads with both first-person and third-person interaction, not an open investigation sandbox.
Many deduction puzzles are satisfying when solved, but some require overly exact input, obscure historical knowledge or unintuitive steps that can prompt consulting a guide.
The authentic-feeling bleak 1888 London setting, murder-case reconstruction and period storytelling are recurring strengths despite dated graphics.
Dated navigation, interaction hotspots, stiff animations and uneven voice performances make the game feel older than its stronger detective ideas.
A roughly ten-hour series of clue-driven scenes gradually builds to the final mystery, although occasional errands and the early stretch can slow the narrative.

An older Russian review praises the local voice performance but says certain deduction puzzles are substantially harder because of translation issues; this does not establish a current universal defect.

Dated English-language reviews disagree about whether a saving and loading bug remained fixed: some describe progress loss, while another reports a 2021 fix. Present technical behaviour is unresolved.

dossiers.title: In Sound Mind
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 9 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: The first-person adventure alternates exploration, searching for tools, environmental puzzles, stealth and shooting, with new mechanics specific to the psychiatric patients' recorded memories.
The psychologist protagonist's patient stories, emotional themes and mystery are often praised, including the way each chapter develops its own fears and motifs.
The Living Tombstone soundtrack, voiced performances and unsettling audio atmosphere enhance the psychological setting in Russian and English player reviews.
Cassette-based chapters explore separate fears and return to a hub where newly found tools open more routes; this produces variety but the pacing is uneven.
Several players find shooting, stealth encounters, cluttered inventory or later combat tedious compared with the more inventive early puzzles and story.
Environmental riddles and platforming are generally approachable but occasionally inventive; generous ammunition and supplies reduce survival pressure for some players.
The adventure's later chapters can feel too long and more action-heavy, making it less consistently frightening than a pure survival horror.
Player accounts include poor optimization, uneven graphics or performance, with reports from different years that do not confirm the current build's technical state.
Changing tools and patient-specific mechanics keep chapters distinct, although repeated shooting and long traversal passages begin to flatten that variety late in the story.

dossiers.title: GRIME
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 9 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: The combat combines stamina-managed dodges, weapons with differing moves and an absorb/parry that destroys exposed enemies and powers healing or learned traits.
Boss rewards unlock traversal techniques and enemy absorption develops passive traits, while strength and dexterity investment changes which weapons become viable.
The connected regions hide optional bosses, passages and rewards behind traversal upgrades; backtracking is frequent and maps may be difficult to orient within.
Fast boss patterns and parry timing reward practice, but some players report sharp difficulty spikes and repeated defeats despite knowing the mechanics.
The grotesque, surreal world, body-horror creatures and sombre audio create a distinctive identity and can motivate players to investigate environmental storytelling.
Sparse travel options, hard-to-read navigation and long routes between destinations make returning through already explored regions less appealing to some players.
New movement techniques and optional secrets encourage revisiting maps, while late platform challenges and repeated boss attempts can exhaust players seeking a smoother journey.
The world's intertwined routes, bosses, secrets and two endings make play exploration-led, rather than a sequence of isolated linear levels.
Some Russian players feel that early build changes and weapon variety are less meaningful than advertised, with limited respec flexibility.
